key_insight: Improving web agents requires practicing the right skills, not just completing more tasks. MiniWeb makes it possible to identify which reusable interaction skills fail, rather than judging agents only by overall task success.
problem_solved: Task-level success rates can hide the specific weaknesses that prevent browser agents from reliably navigating websites, searching for information, and completing transactions.
method: Build MiniWeb, a realistic miniature web with 65 interconnected websites across 15 domains.
Provide 369 human-annotated tasks covering everyday web workflows.
Label 37 reusable interaction primitives across 7 skill families to support skill-level evaluation.
impact: MiniWeb gives practitioners a more actionable way to diagnose web-agent failures and target training toward weak skills. The provided abstract is truncated, so benchmark outcomes and performance gains cannot be established.
visual_elements: Network map showing 65 interconnected websites grouped into 15 domains.
Skill hierarchy organizing 37 interaction primitives into 7 families.
Workflow diagram linking an everyday task to its component interaction skills.
Illustrative skill-level heatmap contrasting detailed failure diagnosis with a single task-success score.
paper_title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
paper_authors: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino
